blocked_leg: user-visible prompt (status-item NSPopover) and therefore model load + plain inference

attempts.detail: process visible; menu bar 1 = '0,0 / 1920,30'; menu bar 2 = '-1,1068 / 20,24' with exactly 1 AXMenuBarItem

frontmost application remained Safari; status item never received the event
frontmost became Finder, i.e. the click landed in the Dock area at the reported AX y=1068
returns [] - window list ownership is not readable without Screen Recording permission

status item reports AXPosition [-1,1068] / AXSize [20,24] while the sole display is 1920x1080 with the menu bar at y=0..30; the reported origin cannot be mapped onto the visible menu bar, so no clickable coordinate can be derived

why_not_worked_around: The only product paths that load a model are the status-item popover (GUI) and the headless SIMIGO_HEADLESS_ROLE entry, which the product itself classifies as restricted_production_path. Driving the headless entry here would substitute a non-user path for stage B instead of evidencing it, so it was not done. No product source, test assertion, authorization requirement or UI element was modified to obtain a pass.
minimal_unblock: Run one human-in-the-loop pass: a person clicks the SimiGo status item once and submits one plain prompt, while this batch captures app log, isolated-home delta, IS rows and the listening socket - this converts the leg from BLOCKED to observed, though it is operator-attested rather than machine-driven.

Or grant the automation host Screen Recording (so CGWindowList/AX window ownership becomes readable) and re-run the coordinate derivation; the AX position defect (-1,1068) may still prevent synthetic clicks.

Or decide, as a product change (not an acceptance bypass), on a supported programmatic entry point that starts the same runtime the popover starts; until such a product entry exists, stage B cannot be driven automatically.
